answer: An orchard gives each agent one tree to tend, with a mirror hung in its branches and a lantern at its roots. Each evening the agent lights the lantern and angles the mirror so the light falls on a marked stone at the end of the row. A warden walks the rows after dark and checks every light spot against the night chart. A tree whose light misses the mark or whose lantern stays dark loses its harvest share for a season. A thousand fake names need a thousand trees, a thousand mirrors angled nightly, and a thousand lanterns kept burning through the night.
